## Finding type

- [ ] Version / release information
- [ ] Screenshot / image
- [ ] Old website / Wayback page
- [ ] README / FAQ / help / documentation
- [ ] EXE / DLL / project-file metadata
- [ ] Hash / package provenance
- [ ] Source-code provenance
- [ ] Developer / community history
- [ ] Duplicate / alternate artifact
- [ ] Correction to an existing archive claim
- [ ] Other

## SubSeven version / branch

Example: `1.9 Apocalypse`, `2.1.3 BONUS`, `2.2`, `2.1.5 Legends`, `2.3`, `Legacy`, or `unknown`.

## Source URL

Original URL, Wayback capture, repository, publication or other public source:

## Date / timeframe

Release date, capture date, publication date, or best-known timeframe:

## What this source demonstrates

Describe the specific historical claim or visual detail supported by the source.

## Artifact details

If relevant, provide:

- Filename:
- File type:
- Size:
- Published hash:
- Duplicate/alternate relationship:

## Screenshot provenance

For screenshots/images, include:

- claimed version:
- original-period / later preservation / retrospective / modern Legacy:
- direct image URL if available:
- what is visibly shown:

## Confidence / uncertainty

What is confirmed, and what remains uncertain?

## Safety check

Do not attach runnable classic malware, directly buildable weaponized classic source, or operational unauthorized-access instructions. Historical metadata, screenshots, readmes, hashes and source links are appropriate.
